questions.stem:
Statements: Q > S = T > R < W.
Conclusions: I. W < R   II. W ≤ Q.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
digital growth rural = su lu mi
digital savings secure = ze su re
growth savings banking = re mi pa
rural secure banking = lu pa ze
digital growth banking = mi su pa
What is the code for “rural”?
questions.explanation: Answer: lu. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: digital = su, growth = mi, rural = lu, savings = re, secure = ze, banking = pa.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 21 km east, turns left and walks 12 km, then turns left and walks 12 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 15. Net displacement is 9 km east and 12 km north. By Pythagoras, √(9² + 12²) = 15 km.

questions.stem: A is the mother of C. F is the son of C. B is the father of C. How is F related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. B is a parent of C, and F is C’s son. Hence F is B’s grandchild.

questions.stem: G is the brother of C. C is the mother of D. B is the father of G and C. How is G related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. G is the brother of D’s mother C. Therefore G is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: E is the only daughter of B. B is the father of E. C is the son of E. D is the sister of B. How is B related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. B is the father of E, and E is C’s mother. Thus B is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 55 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 43. New front rank = 10+3 = 13. Back rank = 55 − 13 + 1 = 43.

questions.stem: In a queue of 36 candidates, a candidate is 15th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 18. New front rank = 15+4 = 19. Back rank = 36 − 19 + 1 = 18.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1400. It is marked above cost and sold at a 20% discount on marked price, earning 25% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 2187.5. Selling price = 1400 × 125/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.8 = 2187.5.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 26 days and B in 39 days. They work together for 2 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 22.67. Use 78 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 78 − 2×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 50 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 10. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 10.

questions.stem: The average of 29 numbers is 45. One number, 57, is replaced and the average rises by 7. What is the new number?

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 4 years, their combined age will be 100 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 69. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 8 = 100; x = 23, so father = 69.
